verdicts.note: The basis says her site cites protecting immigrant communities [S3], but the dossier has no immigration content from S3. What's left is biographical: a founding board role at Hate Free Zone/OneAmerica and an NCSL immigration task force [S1]. The NCSL task force tells us nothing about direction. That is an indirect inference, not a stated position.

Rests on one bill: she signed the committee do-pass report as chair and voted for it on the floor. She has made no statements. ESHB 1296 narrowed I-2081's rights (it swapped curriculum examination for classroom observation, lengthened the records window and cut prior notice of medical services) but kept a parents' rights list. That is a moderate pole_b position. Her role as chair adds confidence, not magnitude. This matches Frame and Street at +1.

The evidence is support for the 2025 rent-increase cap that was already enacted, plus anti-displacement language [S3][S5][S7]. The basis quotes a 'real rent-stabilization cap' that isn't in the dossier. He has no social-housing, right-to-counsel or public-investment proposals, which are the markers of the full pole. Legislators who voted for the same cap (Fitzgibbon, Frame, Street) are at +1.

missing.basis: Criticized the Legislature for giving up about $270M in estate-tax revenue while cutting education ('that doesn't make sense'). Endorsed by Tech 4 Taxes and Fuse Washington. He has no stated position on the millionaires' tax, so +1 rather than +2.
